question: A model has accuracy 0.82 and worse F1. Is the old memo enough?

args.query: model accuracy F1 threshold release approval old memo policy
args.reason: Find the handbook policy about model accuracy/F1 thresholds and whether an old memo suffices.

steps.reasoning: Find the handbook policy about model accuracy/F1 thresholds and whether an old memo suffices.

result.text:
# Legacy release memo — superseded
This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

# Release policy — example company handbook
Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.

# GPU serving — example deployment choices
The planned primary model is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct served by vLLM using BF16 on a 24 GB GPU. For a 12 GB slot use an AWQ quantized model. For a cost comparison use Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Benchmark actual latency and quality before changing production. ONNX conversion is outside this project because vLLM owns the autoregressive decoding and KV cache.

answer.answer: No, the old memo is not enough. The legacy 2024 memo (which promoted any model with accuracy above 0.80) is explicitly superseded and must not be applied. Under the current governing release policy, promotion requires an evaluation on a frozen holdout and is allowed only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. Since this model has accuracy 0.82 but worse F1, it does not meet the current F1-improvement requirement, so the old accuracy-only rule cannot justify promotion. The release approver is the project owner, and the previous production version must be kept for rollback.
